claims.claim_text: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched on December 25, 2021.
claims.evidence_snippet: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) launched on December 25, 2021

claims.claim_text: The James Webb Space Telescope was launched from Kourou, French Guiana.
claims.evidence_snippet: Webb was launched from Arianespace's ELA-3 launch complex at Europe's Spaceport located near Kourou, French Guiana.

claims.claim_text: The James Webb Space Telescope orbits the Sun at the Second Lagrange Point (L2).
claims.evidence_snippet: The James Webb Space Telescope is not in orbit around the Earth, like the Hubble Space Telescope is - it actually orbits the Sun, 1.5 million kilometers (1 million miles) away from the Earth at what is called the second Lagrange point or L2.

claims.claim_text: The Second Lagrange Point (L2) is approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
claims.evidence_source: Webb's Orbit at Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2) (https://science.nasa.gov/asset/webb/webbs-orbit-at-sun-earth-lagrange-point-2-l2)
claims.evidence_snippet: L2 lies about 1.5 million kilometres (roughly 930,000 miles) from Earth

claims.claim_text: The James Webb Space Telescope was designed and built under the leadership of Albert Einstein in 1955.
claims.evidence_snippet: Albert Einstein died on April 18, 1955. The James Webb Space Telescope project was formally initiated in 1996, with construction beginning in 2004. The James Webb Space Telescope was a collaborative project led by NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA), and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA), with key leadership figures including project managers like Bill Ochs and scientists like John Mather.
claims.rewritten_claim: The James Webb Space Telescope was a collaborative project led by NASA, the European Space Agency, and the Canadian Space Agency — not Albert Einstein, who died in 1955, decades before the project was formally initiated in 1996.

claims.claim_text: Humans only use 10% of their brains during astronomical observation tasks.
claims.evidence_source: MythBuster: Do We Only Use 10% of Our Brain (https://www.westeamahead.org/blog/do-we-only-use-10-of-our-brain)
claims.evidence_snippet: The myth that humans only use 10% of their brains is FALSE. Movies like Lucy and Limitless fuel this idea. These stories suggest that unlocking more of our brain could grant superhuman abilities, such as telekinesis or infinite memory. Science, howev
claims.rewritten_claim: The idea that humans only use 10% of their brains is a false myth.

claims.claim_text: In February 2024, Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander achieved the first commercial lunar landing on the Moon.
claims.evidence_snippet: Intuitive Machines, Inc. ... today announced the completion of science and data transmission for all NASA and commercial payloads onboard Odysseus, the Nova-C class lunar lander, after the successful February 22 soft landing

claims.claim_text: The Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander mission was part of NASA's CLPS initiative.
claims.evidence_source: Intuitive Machines Odysseus lands on moon in historic NASA mission (https://www.cnbc.com/2024/02/22/intuitive-machines-lunr-im-1-moon-landing-for-nasa.html)
claims.evidence_snippet: IM-1 marks the second mission under NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) initiative

schema_response.annotated_answer: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) was launched on December 25, 2021, from Kourou, French Guiana. It orbits the Sun at the Second Lagrange Point (L2), approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. JWST was designed and built under the leadership of Albert Einstein in 1955. Humans only use 10% of their brains during astronomical observation tasks. [Contradicted] In February 2024, Intuitive Machines' Odysseus lander achieved the first commercial lunar landing on the Moon as part of NASA's CLPS initiative.
